transcriber_notes: English twin of nodate_vermilion_2012_12_29_fr_e8effd (same pit; chart and table pixel-identical after a (3,-2) px shift, so all measurements carry over; this export also shows the notes panel, cropped from the French one). 713x856 JPEG screenshot of a SnowPro-style Windows form (English labels), no app branding -> source_format 'other'. The screenshot has a horizontal band of ~8 px (~3 cm) cut out around 100 cm: the '100' label is half missing, the 100 cm gridline and the table row line between the '/ □' and padlock rows are gone, and the temperature line has a kink at the cut. Heights were therefore read with the local scale on each side (2.70 px/cm; above the cut 150 cm at y=302, below it 0 at y=699). Boundaries 145/130/55/30/0 from blue bar edges and table lines (+-0.5 cm); the 4F+/1F+ boundary lies inside the removed band (between ~99 and ~102 cm), recorded as 100 and flagged uncertain. Hardness axis geometric (bars grow leftward from the right edge x=325): F/4F/1F/P/K at 13/27/54/108/216 px; bar widths 16 (F+), 33 (4F+), 67 (1F+), 108 (P), 175 (K-); each +/- confirmed by the mark under the R-column hardness symbol. Temperature axis 13.5 px/C, 0 C at x=298 (0 label gridline); circle markers read to +-0.1 C. No marker at the surface (printed surface temp -11.9 not drawn as a point); a marker at 100 cm, if any, was lost in the cut; the 0 cm marker is half clipped by the frame (-1.5). The dashed line from the surface to the top of the axis ends at -8.4 C (air temp, not a snow temperature). Only test info is the notes-panel text; theta (moisture) and HW/rho columns blank. 'Nov 6 rain crust has faceted out' names no height and no layer in the table carries that label, so it stays in header.notes (no date_tag assigned).
